Transcriptional programs and classical signaling pathways are central to bone regulation, where post-translational modifications (PTMs) provide an additional control over the activity, stability, localization, and interactions of proteins involved. This review summarizes current evidence regarding PTMs in bone homeostasis, focusing on their regulatory roles in osteoblast, osteoclast, and osteocyte function under physiological and pathological conditions. We organize the evidence around three concepts: bidirectional interactions between PTMs and classical signaling pathways; functional regulatory modes including signal gating, amplification, and dampening; and spatiotemporal regulation across cell types, subcellular compartments, developmental and aging stages, and disease states. Dysregulated PTMs are associated with osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, metabolic and inflammatory bone diseases, and impaired bone repair. Evidence remains uneven across PTM types and skeletal cell populations, and the causal roles of many site-specific PTM events remain unclear. Emerging methods including quantitative PTM proteomics, single-cell and spatial analyses, and multi-omics approaches are beginning to address these limitations. We hope that combining PTM evidence with established signaling pathways will deepen the understanding of bone homeostasis and identify which issues require further experimental validation.

title: Temporal drift, calibration monitoring, and adaptive updating of an IVIG resistance prediction model in Kawasaki disease: a multicenter pediatric cohort study
abstract: Background: Clinical prediction models can lose accuracy over time as case mix and clinical environments change, but evidence on temporal drift and model updating in pediatric prediction models remains limited. We evaluated temporal drift in a multicenter prediction model for intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) resistance in Kawasaki disease (KD) and assessed whether half-life-weighted updating might help maintain performance over time. Methods: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study including children with KD treated between 2006 and 2024. A baseline model was developed in the pre-COVID cohort (2006–2019) and temporally validated in the during-COVID (2020–2022) and after-COVID (2023–2024) cohorts. Five algorithms were compared, and Elastic Net was selected for further evaluation. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. Updating strategies included recalibration, cumulative refitting, and half-life-weighted updating. Findings: Among 6443 children with KD, 3788 were in the pre-COVID cohort, 1837 in the during-COVID cohort, and 818 in the after-COVID cohort; IVIG resistance occurred in 22.3%, 32.8%, and 12.8% of cases, respectively. Elastic Net showed the best temporal performance. Discrimination declined from an AUC of 0.846 during COVID to 0.703 after COVID. Calibration drift was more pronounced, with progressive underestimation of risk across periods. Recalibration and cumulative refitting only partly stabilized performance. Half-life-weighted updating showed modest improvement, and half-lives of 3–4 years provided a relatively balanced performance. Interpretation: This pediatric prediction model for IVIG resistance in KD showed temporal drift over time, particularly in calibration. Static deployment might be insufficient for long-term use in temporally changing settings.

title: International Delphi on a medical screening tool for emergency department patients with psychiatric complaints
authors: and the Delphi Informed Medical Evaluation (DIME) study group
abstract: Abstract Background: Medical screening in the emergency department (ED) is performed to identify underlying medical conditions that may contribute to a patient’s psychiatric presentation and/or require treatment. This process frequently causes disagreement between emergency physicians and psychiatrists regarding objectives and scope of medical screening, leading to potentially unnecessary testing, prolonged ED length-of-stay, and increased costs. This study aims to develop an evidence-informed and consensus-based medical screening tool through a transdisciplinary, international Delphi process. Methods: This modified international Delphi study was conducted between May and November 2025 using a 4-round modified Delphi process with online surveys and online steering committee discussions. Participants included 25 society representatives from 7 emergency medicine and psychiatry societies across 4 continents and 6 patient representatives with prior ED medical screening experience as patients or patient relatives. Participants generated, rated, refined, and reached consensus on proposed screening elements. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement in Round 3. In Round 4, the resulting tool was applied to 37 standardized clinical vignettes. Interrater agreement was assessed using Gwet agreement coefficient (AC). Results: Of 28 invited society representatives and steering committee members, 25 (89.3%) participated in Round 1, 23 (82.1%) in Round 2, 22 (78.6%) in Round 3, and 23 (82.1%) in Round 4. The 6 patient representatives completed all 4 rounds. In Round 1, participants generated 91 statements from society representatives and 27 from patient representatives. Following refinement in Round 2, consensus in Round 3 was achieved for 48 of 91 society representatives’ statements (52.8%) and 21 of 27 patient statements (77.8%), which were synthesized into the Delphi-Informed Medical Evaluation (DIME) tool. In Round 4, application of the draft DIME tool to 37 clinical vignettes demonstrated almost perfect agreement among society representatives (Gwet AC, 0.86; 95%-CI 0.78–0.93; p < .001) and substantial agreement among patient representatives (Gwet AC, 0.76; 95%-CI 0.66–0.86; p < .001). Conclusions This international modified Delphi study developed the DIME tool, a consensus-based medical screening tool to identify adult ED patients with psychiatric complaints who are at low risk for acute medical illness. Prospective multicenter validation studies are required before clinical implementation. Trial registration clinicaltrials.gov, NCT06936826

title: Early-life risk factors and cardiometabolic outcomes in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Importance Childhood obesity increases cardiometabolic risk during childhood among individuals aged 2-18 years. These cardiometabolic outcomes include glucose intolerance, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). In the current state of research, a comprehensive review identifying all early-life exposures and risk factors that could predict cardiometabolic risk in children is lacking. Objective To identify and evaluate the predictive early-life risk factors during the first 1,000 days of life, including preconception, pregnancy and birth, and early infancy periods for cardiometabolic risk outcomes in childhood. Evidence review The present systematic review of existing literature was conducted to revise and search selected electronic databases (Medline, EMBASE, WEB OF SCIENCE, SCOPUS, and Cochrane CENTRAL) for longitudinal studies published between the database’s inception and August 17 , 2022. This systematic review protocol was registered to PROSPERO, CRD42022355152, and following the PRISMA guidelines. We selected articles that studied the risk factors in mothers, fathers and infants, from preconception to infancy, for childhood cardiometabolic outcomes between 2 and 18 years. Findings In 68 studies, we identified 229 associations between exposures and childhood cardiometabolic outcomes namely glucose intolerance, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, and T2D. The majority of associations (n=162) were positively associated with cardiometabolic risk factors. Pregnancy and birth risk factors were the categories with the most reported associations (86%). Among them, the most frequently assessed characteristics were birth anthropometrics (n=75), sociodemographics data (n=47), and pregnancy complications factors (n=34). However, we only identified few risk factors during preconception. In infancy period, breastfeeding (n=16) and infant anthropometrics (n=15) were consistently associated with cardiometabolic outcomes. In all periods, the most studied associations were identified for hypertension and metabolic syndrome. Conclusions and relevance Birth anthropometrics, sociodemographics, and pregnancy complication factors were the most frequently reported predictive factors associated with a higher risk for cardiometabolic outcomes in children, particularly hypertension and metabolic syndrome. These results of this study are useful for predicting the risk for childhood cardiometabolic outcomes and for the modifiable factors. They also may facilitate the design of approaches aimed at the alteration of several behaviours from birth to infancy, encompassing both the maternal and paternal influences, as well as the preconception to infancy transition period. Future studies evaluating early-life risk factors with scarce scientific evidence, such as paternal and preconception factors, are urgently needed. Key points Question What is the existing evidence of early-life risk factors during the first 1000 days of life that are associated with cardiometabolic dysfunction between 2 and 18 years? Findings Birth anthropometrics, pregnancy complications, sociodemographics and lifestyle factors are the most frequently reported associated exposures with hypertension and metabolic syndrome in children. Meaning Identifying early-life risk factors and changing behavior patterns throughout preconception and infancy can contribute to prevent metabolic diseases later in childhood.

title: Associations between behavioral intervention dose and outcomes in children and adolescents with obesity: meta-regression of randomized clinical trials
abstract: Background: Childhood obesity is a growing global health challenge with long-term consequences. Behavioral interventions are pivotal in the management of obesity, yet the relationship between intervention dose and effectiveness remains controversial.

title: Associations of short-term ambient temperature and directional temperature change with cardiovascular admissions among older adults: a time-stratified case-crossover study
abstract: Older adults are particularly vulnerable to the cardiovascular effects of short-term ambient temperature exposure. However, evidence remains limited on the lagged, non-linear associations of daily mean temperature and short-term directional temperature change with cardiovascular hospital admissions among large populations of older adults. We conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study among adults aged 65 years or older in Henan Province, China, from 2019 to 2024. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) admissions were identified from inpatient discharge records and linked to elderly health management rosters. Environmental exposures were assigned using the geocoded locations of participants’ affiliated primary healthcare institutions as exposure-location proxies. Distributed lag non-linear models were used to estimate cumulative and lag-specific associations between daily mean temperature and CVD admissions over lag days 0–14. We additionally examined short-term directional temperature change within the lag 0–3-day window after adjustment for concurrent mean temperature, relative humidity, and fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅). A total of 8,876,140 older adults were identified, of whom 8,875,258 were assigned exposure-location proxies. The primary CVD analysis included 2,598,149 admission events and 11,424,206 case-day and control-day records. The cumulative temperature-admission curve was non-linear. Relative to the temperature at which the fitted cumulative exposure-response function was minimized (28.5 °C), the odds ratio (OR) was 1.032 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.009–1.056) at − 3.6 °C and 1.064 (95% CI, 1.045–1.084) at 0.2 °C; the fitted maximum was approximately 14.2 °C (OR, 1.194; 95% CI, 1.177–1.213), and the OR was 1.015 (95% CI, 1.003–1.027) at 32.0 °C. At 0.2 °C, the association emerged after approximately 2 days and persisted through lag day 14, whereas the association at 32.0 °C was smaller and more immediate. After adjustment for concurrent mean temperature, directional warming was also associated with CVD admissions (OR, 1.030; 95% CI, 1.023–1.038 at + 8.5 °C). Temperature-admission associations varied across the temperature range and by lag, whereas the directional-warming association was small and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Because absolute admission risk and attributable burden were not estimated, the clinical and public health relevance remains uncertain.

title: Biologically informed network-regularized sparse consensus clustering (BioNet-SPACC) identifies a continuous plasma proteomic axis in major depressive disorder
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional case-control analyses may obscure continuous molecular variation. We developed biologically informed network-regularized sparse consensus clustering (BioNet-SPACC), integrating protein-protein interaction priors with sparse feature weighting in a leakage-controlled discovery and held-out test design. BioNet-SPACC was applied to 4,123 UK Biobank participants with MDD, divided into discovery and held-out test samples. Propensity-matched healthy controls (HCs) were introduced after MDD-only discovery for anchoring. Analyses assessed clustering stability, held-out concordance, and dimensional structure. A locked 15-protein panel was assessed in a non-overlapping UK Biobank Wave 3 MDD sample ( n = 42) for exploratory cross-wave concordance. An independent plasma LC-MS/MS dataset comprising 38 participants with MDD and 40 HCs was used for exploratory cross-platform comparison at the pathway level. BioNet-SPACC identified an internally stable K = 2 partition (median ARI = 0.986) defined by a Core 85 protein signature. The partition identified low-axis and high-axis operational groups positioned along a dominant continuous proteomic dimension. PC1 explained 91.3% of the variance in the Core 85 representation, and complementary distributional analyses provided no evidence against unimodality. In the held-out test sample, de novo clustering agreed with discovery-projected assignments (ARI = 0.789; NMI = 0.742; κ = 0.888), despite partial overlap in selected proteins (Jaccard = 0.417). CBC conditioning strongly preserved continuous molecular-axis scores within MDD (Pearson r = 0.940), whereas binary assignments showed moderate agreement with the primary solution. On the HC-standardized centroid-defined molecular-axis score, the overall MDD and HC means were similar (Cohen’s d = 0.01), whereas the low-axis and high-axis MDD groups occupied opposing positions relative to HCs. CBC and NMR analyses identified peripheral correlates spanning platelet-related hematological and metabolic traits. The 15-protein panel recovered discovery-derived assignments in held-out data (AUC = 0.997) and showed preliminary within-UKB, same-platform cross-wave concordance. These findings support a reproducible, predominantly continuous peripheral proteomic axis within MDD. BioNet-SPACC integrates PPI-informed regularization with sparse consensus clustering to provide a biologically informed framework for reproducible molecular structure discovery in high-dimensional proteomic data.

title: Comparative effectiveness of first-/second-generation EGFR-TKI combination therapy versus third-generation EGFR-TKI monotherapy in untreated locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutant NSCLC: a real-world, retrospective study in China
abstract: Third-generation (3G) epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are recommended first-line options for advanced EGFR -mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In real-world practice, first- or second-generation (1G/2G) EGFR-TKI combination strategies remain frequently used, particularly where access to 3G EGFR-TKIs is limited by cost or reimbursement. As of October 2024, first-line osimertinib was not routinely reimbursed in five Asian countries. Direct real-world comparisons of these two strategies are limited. This retrospective study enrolled previously-untreated patients with stage III/IV EGFR -mutant NSCLC from January 2017 to December 2023. Propensity-score matching (PSM, 1:2) balanced baseline characteristics between patients receiving 1G/2G EGFR-TKI combination therapy or 3G EGFR-TKI monotherapy. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR). Of 512 eligible patients, 364 were included after PSM. Median PFS was longer with 3G EGFR-TKI monotherapy than with 1G/2G TKI combination therapy (20.5 vs. 16.0 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.50–0.80; P < 0.001). The PFS benefit was observed in both sexes, smoking statuses, and stages III/IV, and among the aged, those with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0–1, adenocarcinoma or EGFR exon 19 deletion, and no baseline brain metastases. Median OS did not differ significantly between 3G EGFR-TKI and 1G/2G TKI combination group (46.1 vs. 41.6 months; HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.72–1.26; P = 0.721). In the combination group, 165 patients (70.5%) received 3G EGFR-TKIs in later lines and had longer OS than those who did not. ORR (63.1% vs. 59.6%; P = 0.498) and DCR (99.2% vs. 99.5%; P = 0.903) were similar between groups. Adverse event-related discontinuation and dose reduction were more frequent with combination therapy. First-line 3G EGFR-TKI monotherapy was associated with longer PFS than 1G/2G EGFR-TKI combination therapy. The lack of statistically significant OS difference may partly reflect subsequent 3G EGFR-TKIs use after progression. These findings support 3G EGFR-TKIs as preferred first-line options when accessible. For selected patients, 1G/2G EGFR-TKI combination therapy may remain an alternative in settings with limited reimbursement or high costs.

title: Evaluating the functional impact of yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation following percutaneous coronary intervention
abstract: Yoga may offer a holistic, accessible and sustainable approach to cardiac rehabilitation (CR). However, randomized data evaluating its role in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who have undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is limited. The aim of this trial was to evaluate the efficacy of yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation compared to standard care in patients following PCI for acute or chronic coronary syndromes. Adults who had recently undergone PCI for acute or chronic coronary syndrome were randomized to a structured yoga-based CR program ( n = 98) or standard care ( n = 102). The primary endpoint was a change in exercise capacity (maximally tolerated exercise duration on treadmill testing using Bruce protocol) at 6 months. Key secondary endpoints included patient reported quality of life assessed via the WHO-BREF tool, patient reported physical activity level measured using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and rates of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). 200 patients with revascularized coronary artery disease with a median age of 53 years and male preponderance (87%, 174 male patients) were randomized to yoga-based rehabilitation or standard care. There was no significant difference in maximal exercise duration on treadmill testing at 6 months in the intention- to - treat analysis (7 [5, 8.2] vs. 6.32 [5.1, 8.1] minutes, p = 0.449). At 6 months, the yoga-based CR group demonstrated significant improvements in the domains of physical health ( p < 0.001), psychological health ( p < 0.001), and environment ( p = 0.007) (WHO-BREF quality of life questionnaire), lower anxiety ( p = 0.002) and stress scores ( p = 0.024) and higher self-reported physical activity levels (median METS: 1697.5 [742.5, 2631.75] vs. 500.25 [0, 1027.12], p < 0.001). The Yoga-CR compliant group (per-protocol analysis) suggested better maximal exercise duration on treadmill testing (7.01 [4.41, 8.14] vs. 7.12 [6.28, 9.05] minutes, p = 0.03) at 6 months. Yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation following percutaneous coronary intervention improved quality of life, self-reported physical activity, and psychological outcomes at 6 months compared with standard care. Although no significant improvement in exercise capacity was observed in primary intention-to-treat analysis, the findings support yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation as a complementary strategy to conventional cardiac rehabilitation, with intervention adherence appearing to be an important determinant of functional improvement. The trial was prospectively registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2017/07/008951).

title: Neoadjuvant toripalimab plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction: a phase II trial
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus surgery is for the treatment of locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction (AEG), yet pathological response remains suboptimal. Given the potential synergy between PD-1 blockade and radiotherapy in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment, we hypothesized that adding toripalimab, a PD-1 inhibitor, to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy could improve tumor response. We enrolled cT3-T4/N + M0 AEG patients in this prospective, single-arm, phase II trial. Patients received neoadjuvant radiotherapy (50 Gy/45 Gy/25 f), with 5 cycles of weekly chemotherapy concurrently and 4 cycles of toripalimab, followed by radical surgery and adjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. The primary endpoint was the major pathological response (MPR) rate; the secondary endpoints included the pathological complete response (pCR) rate, R0 resection rate, disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS) and safety, with exploratory analyses of immune correlates including the tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS). Between September 1, 2019, and April 30, 2024, 40 patients were enrolled. Thirty-one patients underwent radical surgery. In the surgery population, R0 resection rate was 100%, 24 patients (77.4%) achieved an MPR, and the pCR rate was 41.9%. In terms of safety, only one case of ≥ grade 4 treatment-related toxicity and one case of ≥ grade 3 surgical complication were reported. Notably, pCR patients were more likely to have detectable TLSs ( p = 0.047). During a median follow-up period of 54.4 months for OS and 51.6 months for DFS, the surgery set had 2-year and 4-year OS rates of 93.5% and 86.6%, versus 85.0% and 71.5% in the whole population. The 2-year and 4-year DFS rates of the surgery cohort were 83.9% and 80.4% respectively. Neoadjuvant toripalimab combined with chemoradiotherapy demonstrates promising efficacy and manageable toxicity in locally advanced AEG, with a notable association between TLS and pathological response. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04061928 in August 2019.

title: How to tackle inequities in bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities: a national qualitative study using experience-based co-design
abstract: BACKGROUND: High-income countries globally are becoming increasingly diverse. People from ethnically diverse communities experience inequities in accessing bereavement support, but evidence to inform equitable provision remains limited. We aimed to determine how formal bereavement support services can better serve ethnically diverse communities by identifying barriers to and facilitators of equitable access, defining key components of culturally safe and appropriate bereavement care, and developing a logic model and recommendations for equitable bereavement support. METHODS: Multi-phase national qualitative study, drawing on experience-based co-design principles. We conducted interviews (n = 53) and focus groups (n = 9) with 121 bereaved people from 13 ethnically diverse backgrounds, interviews with 23 bereavement support providers across 12 services, four online co-design workshops with bereaved people and stakeholders (n = 53), and a hybrid workshop to refine recommendations (n = 29 stakeholders). Recruitment and data collection prioritised cultural safety and an asset-based approach. Directed thematic analysis was informed by Levesque et al.'s access to healthcare framework. RESULTS: Barriers to equitable bereavement support arose across the access pathway but were concentrated mainly within bereavement support organisations and the wider bereavement support system. Racism and intersectionality were cross-cutting themes, influencing whether bereaved people could identify, trust, reach and engage with support. Key barriers included poor signposting and referral, long waiting lists, limited staff diversity, language barriers, weak organisational commitment to equity, precarious funding, and white-centred, individualised models of grief support. Participants identified culturally safe and equitable care as requiring anti-racist practice, sustained community partnership, provision of support in trusted settings and community languages, holistic and flexible provision, and greater investment in grassroots services designed and delivered by ethnically diverse communities. The logic model and recommendations identify system-wide actions needed to address barriers and support equitable access. CONCLUSIONS: Inequitable access to bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities is rooted primarily in the design, organisation and cultural orientation of services and the wider bereavement support system. Improving equity will require sustained investment in community-led provision, accountability mechanisms, and genuine partnership with ethnically diverse communities. Findings from this robust multi-perspective study provide actionable recommendations to reform bereavement support across high- and middle-income settings.

title: Local circuitry mechanisms underlying motor cortex stimulation for chronic pain treatment
abstract: Abstract Chronic pain remains a global challenge with limited therapeutic options. Motor cortex stimulation (MCS), encompassing invasive and non-invasive forms, has emerged as an effective neuromodulatory intervention in specific chronic pain types, yet its neurocircuitry mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Understanding local circuitry mechanisms underlying primary motor cortex (M1) activation is fundamental to achieving a comprehensive understanding of its neurocircuitry mechanisms and its involvement in the treatment of pain. This Review synthesizes translational evidence, specifically focusing on clinical electrophysiological findings, to propose a local circuitry framework for MCS-related analgesia. Drawing on mechanistic insights into M1 neuroanatomy and neuroplasticity, we characterize modality-specific engagement patterns of the local microcircuitry for enhanced motor cortical outputs and delineate the neurobiological mechanisms underlying synaptic plasticity alterations within the M1 microcircuitry responsible for sustained pain relief. Leveraging these mechanisms, we propose precision strategies across spatial, temporal, and personalized dimensions to optimize clinical outcomes. This synthesis bridges molecular, cellular, and circuit-level insights to accelerate the efficacy of mechanism-guided therapeutics for refractory pain.

title: Early-to-mid-pregnancy maternal free thyroxine and fetal growth velocity trajectories: evidence from a large prospective cohort
abstract: Early pregnancy is a critical period for fetal development. Isolated hypothyroxinemia has been reported in 4.2–8.8% of women in Chinese early-pregnancy cohorts, yet population-level evidence linking maternal thyroid hormone status to longitudinal fetal growth trajectories remains limited. We analysed 69,675 singleton pregnancies from a prospective cohort. Maternal free thyroxine (FT4), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) were assessed in the first or second trimester. Fetal growth velocities were derived from 324,886 ultrasound observations obtained between 13 and 41 gestational weeks, including head circumference (HC), abdominal circumference (AC), femur length (FL), biparietal diameter (BPD), and estimated fetal weight (EFW). Growth restriction patterns (cephalic, head-sparing, selective, symmetrical) were defined using population-based 10th percentiles. Linear mixed-effects models assessed velocity associations, while mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression evaluated pattern associations. Higher maternal FT4 was associated with modestly higher fetal growth velocities across all biometric parameters, with estimated EFW velocity differences of 3.07 (95% CI 2.88, 3.26) g/week between the 10th and 90th percentiles of FT4, and with lower odds of cephalic, head-sparing, and symmetrical restriction patterns (all P < 0.001). Hypothyroxinemia was associated with slower fetal growth velocities (all P < 0.001) and increased odds of symmetrical restriction (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.37, 2.26). Exploratory interaction analyses suggested heterogeneity in the associations of hypothyroxinemia with HC, AC, FL, and BPD velocities according to TPOAb status. Maternal FT4 and hypothyroxinemia were associated with fetal growth velocities and selected growth restriction phenotypes in this large longitudinal cohort. These findings indicate modest population-level associations between maternal thyroid hormone status and fetal growth trajectories, while the clinical relevance of these differences requires further investigation.

title: Identification of known potential confounders to design target trial emulation studies: a systematic assessment
abstract: Abstract Background We aimed to systematically identify and assess known potential confounders for the design of a target trial emulation on multiple sclerosis and to investigate its feasibility. Methods We used the comparison of two drugs for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. We conducted a systematic literature analysis (date of last search November 2, 2023) of observational studies and randomized trials, qualitative interviews, and a quantitative survey with clinicians. All identified potential confounders were categorized and classified by clinical importance. We estimated the resource use per study step and per identified potential confounder. Results We assessed 53 observational studies and 27 randomized trials, surveyed 8 clinicians, and conducted 8 interviews with clinical experts. We identified a total of 160 individual potential confounders. While most of these were identified in the literature ( n = 125, 78%), interviews revealed an additional 35 (22%) factors. Of the 17 confounders rated by clinicians as very important for treatment decisions, 9 were identified by interviews (53%). All the potential confounders related to patient perspective were identified in interviews only. Across all data sources, the 5 most frequently considered factors were age ( n = 71), gender/sex ( n = 62), disability status ( n = 62), disease duration ( n = 53), and relapses ( n = 44); these were all considered in 16 (30%) of the observational studies. Sixty-two person-days were deemed necessary to identify the 160 potential confounders. Conclusions There was a substantial discrepancy between factors considered when making treatment decisions and the confounders considered in studies. Even with extensive efforts, it is likely that for observational studies assessing treatment effects their key assumption of no unmeasured confounding is currently not met, and they will have challenges to provide credible real-world evidence due to serious concerns of confounding bias.

title: Adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy in completely resected non–small cell lung cancer with major uncommon EGFR mutations: a real-world study
abstract: The clinical benefit of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in patients with completely resected non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring major uncommon EGFR mutations remains uncertain. We evaluated the efficacy of adjuvant EGFR-TKIs and explored outcomes according to TKI generation and mutation subtype. Patients with completely resected NSCLC harboring major uncommon EGFR mutations, including G719X, S768I, L861Q, or compound major uncommon mutations, treated between 2020 and 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients receiving adjuvant EGFR-TKIs were compared with those managed without TKIs. Baseline imbalances were adjusted using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Disease-free survival (DFS) was the primary endpoint. Among 154 eligible patients, 46 (29.9%) received adjuvant EGFR-TKIs and 108 (70.1%) did not. Median follow-up was 45.1 months (interquartile range 33.5–58.3). After IPTW adjustment, adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy was associated with improved 3-year DFS compared with no TKI therapy (73.6% vs. 53.0%; p = 0.018). Multivariable Cox analysis identified adjuvant TKI therapy as an independent protective factor for DFS (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.42; p = 0.006). The association appeared more evident in patients with stage III disease (hazard ratio: 0.26; p = 0.006). Third-generation TKIs were associated with longer DFS than earlier-generation agents (3-year DFS 83.7% vs. 52.7%; p = 0.010). Adjuvant EGFR-TKIs were associated with prolonged DFS in completely resected NSCLC with major uncommon EGFR mutations. The observed benefit appeared more pronounced in stage III disease and among patients receiving third-generation TKIs. These findings are exploratory and support prospective evaluation of adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy in this rare molecular subgroup.

title: Network-level convergence of functional and structural alterations in first-episode major depressive disorder
abstract: Understanding network-level neuropathological alterations in first-episode major depressive disorder (FED) is essential for clarifying early-stage depression mechanisms. Although numerous studies have investigated FED, reported findings remain highly heterogeneous. We systematically reviewed functional and structural neuroimaging studies comparing patients with FED and healthy individuals, extracting coordinates of reported group differences. Coordinate-level coordinate network mapping (CNM), combined with a normative connectome dataset ( n = 1,000), was applied to derive FED-associated functional and structural networks. These networks were mapped onto canonical large-scale brain networks to provide a functional interpretation within established systems. Cross-modal overlap and spatial correspondence between functional and structural networks were quantified to evaluate their cross-modal alignment. Separately, spatial associations with neurotransmitter distribution maps were examined to contextualize potential neurochemical alterations in FED. Robustness was evaluated using alternative seed sizes, test–retest data, and study-level CNM. Specificity was examined using parallel CNM analyses of first-episode schizophrenia (FES) and drug-naïve obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD), and sensitivity was assessed using drug-naïve FED samples and leave-one-study-out analyses. Eighty-two studies (4,480 FED and 4,211 controls) revealed convergent FED-associated networks involving the hippocampus, insula, thalamus, precuneus, temporal cortex, middle frontal gyrus, and cingulate cortex. The identified FED-associated networks showed a systematic network organization: the functional network predominantly aligned with the cingulo-opercular, somatomotor, and posterior multimodal networks, whereas the structural network primarily aligned with the default mode, auditory, and language networks. FED-associated probability maps across two modalities showed strong whole-brain correspondence ( r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Furthermore, significant spatial associations were observed between FED-associated probability maps and several neurotransmitter systems, including the dopamine transporter, N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptor, and vesicular acetylcholine transporter. The identified networks were highly consistent across seed sizes, test–retest data, drug-naïve samples, and leave-one-study-out analyses, and showed relatively limited spatial overlap with FES- and OCD-associated networks. Comparison with study-level CNM demonstrated high whole-brain spatial correspondence but differences in the detailed topology of the functional network. By integrating heterogeneous neuroimaging evidence, CNM delineates a coherent large-scale network architecture underlying FED. These findings refine the system-level characterization of early-stage depression and may help inform future neuromodulation strategies.

title: Longitudinal associations of hormone therapy and depressive symptoms in cognitively unimpaired older women
abstract: Abstract Background Women are disproportionately affected by depressive disorders relative to men, and mid-life differences like menopause can exacerbate symptoms. Hormone therapy (HT) is a common treatment to ease menopause transitions, including vasomotor and depressive symptoms, that may occur due to menopause-related hormonal changes, but its effects on later-life depressive symptoms remain unclear. Our objective was to examine the association between self-reported post-menopausal HT use and longitudinal changes in depressive symptoms in cognitively unimpaired age-matched older men and women from the Harvard Aging Brain Study and affiliated studies, along with sub-analyses examining interactions with Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) risk factors and neuroimaging markers. Methods Linear mixed-effect models examined the relationship between HT use and changes in the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). Secondary analyses tested the moderating effects of apolipoprotein ε4 ( APOE ε4) status, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), amyloid-β (Aβ) status, medial temporal lobe tau, and hippocampal volume on the association between HT and GDS scores over time. Results In a sample of 585 individuals (58.3% women, Age = 71.6 (+ 7.72 SD)), 42% of women reported current or past HT use. 7% of women self-reported mild to moderate depressive symptoms at baseline (GDS = 11–19). Female HT users reported significantly greater depressive symptoms over time relative to age-matched men (β = 0.11; 95% CI:-0.22- -0.01; p = 0.03) even after adjusting for history of depressive episodes, but not different relatively to female non-users (β=-0.10; 95% CI:-0.21- 0.01; p = 0.07). WMH volume moderated the relationship between HT use and changing depressive symptoms, with female HT users reported greater depressive symptoms over time relative to men (β=-0.09; 95% CI:-0.18- -0.01; p = 0.03) in the setting of high WMH volume, but not relative to female non-users (β=-0.06; 95% CI:-0.15–0.04; p = 0.28). Moderating effects of Aβ, medial temporal lobe tau, and hippocampal volume were not significant. Conclusions In the overall group, female HT users and female non-users did not differ in changes in depression scores. However, female HT users exhibited subtly greater depressive symptoms over time relative to men and WMH moderated this relationship. This underscores the importance of investigating menopausal treatment factors that may affect depressive symptoms in older women and to understand their relationship with white matter lesions.

title: Primary hyperparathyroidism across the care continuum: gaps in diagnosis, access to surgery, and post-operative care
abstract: Abstract Background PHPT (primary hyperparathyroidism) is a common endocrine disorder characterised by inappropriate elevation of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and hypercalcaemia, leading to multisystem complications, including skeletal fragility, nephrolithiasis, neurocognitive impairment, and cardiovascular risks. Despite the availability of curative parathyroidectomy (surgical removal of overactive parathyroid gland(s)), many patients experience delayed diagnosis and inequitable access to surgery. Main text Diagnostic delay in PHPT is driven by inconsistent application of testing guidelines, limited use of ionised calcium, biochemical masking by vitamin D deficiency, age-related diagnostic ambiguity, patient and clinician unawareness of the condition, and reliance on fixed calcium thresholds, resulting in frequent incidental diagnosis and a substantial proportion of patients remaining undiagnosed despite biochemical evidence. Surgical referral is often restricted by arbitrary serum calcium cut-offs and age-based differential criteria, even though evidence demonstrates that timely surgery improves outcomes across age groups. Recognition of PHPT as a systemic disorder extending beyond classical skeletal and renal manifestations highlights the need to consider its broader clinical spectrum, including neurocognitive symptoms and other potential systemic manifestations. Postoperative care remains insufficiently addressed, yet persistent and recurrent PHP require long-term biochemical monitoring, and skeletal recovery require structured follow-up. Conclusions Timely recognition of PHPT and equitable access to curative parathyroidectomy are essential to reduce disease burden and prevent avoidable morbidity. Greater clinical awareness of the broader clinical spectrum of PHPT, improved diagnostic and referral pathways, and stronger evidence on disease trajectories, treatment response, and long-term follow-up are needed to address persistent gaps across the PHPT care continuum.

title: Genetic and environmental influences on rotator cuff tears: a population-based twin study
abstract: Abstract Background Rotator cuff tear (RCT) is a leading cause of shoulder pain, disability, and healthcare utilization worldwide, imposing notable individual and societal burden. Despite its high prevalence and impact on quality of life and healthcare costs, the contribution of inherited susceptibility to clinically manifest RCT remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide, population-based twin study by linking the Danish Twin Registry with the Danish National Patient Registry, including all monozygotic (MZ) and dizygotic (DZ) twin pairs born 1940–1980 and alive on January 1st, 1980. RCT cases between 1994 and 2014 were identified using relevant ICD-8 and ICD-10 codes. Cumulative incidence of receiving an RCT diagnosis was estimated, and familial aggregation was assessed using casewise concordance. Genetic and environmental contributions to liability were quantified using biometric twin models. Results By age 70, the population-based cumulative incidence of RCT was higher in men (6.5%, 95% CI: 6.0%–7.2%) than in women (3.8%, 95% CI: 3.4%–4.3%). The risk of RCT in a twin given RCT in the co-twin was generally higher in MZ than in DZ twins overall, most clearly among men, indicating familial aggregation consistent with genetic effects. In the full cohort, the preferred biometric model (AE) indicated that approximately half the variance in liability to RCT was attributable to additive genetic effects ( heritability : a 2 = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27–0.70), with the remainder due to unique environmental effects ( e 2 = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.30–0.73). Sex-stratified analyses suggested a stronger genetic contribution among men, whereas estimates among women were less precise. Conclusions These findings support clinically diagnosed rotator cuff tear as a common, partially heritable musculoskeletal disorder and highlight the importance of considering individual susceptibility alongside occupational and environmental exposures in prevention, with implications for population-level risk assessment and clinical management.

title: Clinical trial data transparency should match data access to scientific purpose: a tiered framework for reproducibility and reuse
abstract: Abstract Background Clinical trial data sharing is increasingly endorsed by journals, funders, regulators, and research organisations. Nevertheless, access to individual participant data (IPD) remains inconsistent and may not be available when trial results are published. Access timelines can reflect several distinct components, including scientific and governance review, contractual and legal procedures, data preparation, de-identification, transfer, and subsequent harmonisation. When original data are unavailable, researchers may reconstruct approximate participant-level event-time data from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Trinquart and Stockler recently proposed that trialists instead release minimal analysable time-to-event data at publication. Their proposal raises a broader question: what kinds of data and documentation are required for different forms of reproducibility and scientific reuse? Main text We argue that clinical trial data transparency should be considered in relation to the scientific claims and research activities that a particular data object can support. We propose a three-tier framework for data intentionally released or made accessible by trialists or data custodians. Tier 1 comprises original publication-time reduced datasets and supports endpoint-level numerical reproducibility and analyses that are functions of the released observations. Tier 2 comprises reproducibility packages containing analysis-ready data, code, derivation logic, and documentation sufficient to reproduce the reported analytic process. Tier 3 provides governed access to broader de-identified IPD for substantively new analyses and reassessment of operational and analytic decisions. Reconstructed pseudo-IPD are considered separately because they are generated externally from publications rather than shared from the trial database. Privacy protection, governance, and processing environment are cross-cutting dimensions and do not map uniquely to a particular tier. They also apply differently to each tier. Conclusions Publication-time reduced datasets can provide meaningful and timely transparency when broader IPD are not yet accessible. Their value should be recognised without confusing endpoint-level numerical reproducibility with reproduction of the complete analytic process or broader scientific reuse. We propose that publication-time reduced datasets should form a practical floor for timely transparency, while reproducibility packages and governed access to broader IPD provide progressively richer opportunities for reproducing, interrogating, and extending clinical trial analyses.

title: Indole induces intestinal T helper-17 cell overproduction during inflammatory bowel disease through PKA/SP1-mediated Trim21 transcription
abstract: Gut microbiota induce intestinal Th17 cells in both physiological and disease states, yet whether there are shared mechanisms remains unclear. We previously identified the Fbxw7-Trim21 axis as critical for Alcaligenes faecalis -driven physiological Th17 differentiation. Here, we reveal its dual role in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-associated Th17 cell induction. The IBD model was adopted by DSS-induced acute colitis, TNBS-induced acute colitis, Il10 −/− chronic mice and Rag1 −/− mice transferred with CD4 + T cell chronic colitis. Fbxw7 fl/fl , dLck-Cre , Rag1 −/− , Il10 −/− , Il17a GFP and Trim21 −/− mice were used in this paper. Mechanistic studies used molecular and multiomics approaches. mEVs/αCD4/TΔR were constructed by coincubation at 37 °C for 3 h. Dubosiella newyorkensis ( D. newyorkensis ) were colonized to prevent IBD. Key findings were validated in DSS-induced colitis by orally mEVs/αCD4/TΔR treatment or D. newyorkensis colonized. Indole from IBD-gut microbiota reinforces the interaction between protein kinase PKA and transcription factor SP1, promoting SP1 phosphorylation and activation. Then, SP1 induces more E3 ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7 degradation by promoting E3 ubiquitin ligase Trim21 transcription, causing Th17 cell overproduction. Tryptophan-rich feeding enhances Indole production, aggravating IBD, while D. newyorkensis colonization alleviates IBD by shifting tryptophan catabolism toward Kynurenine. Furthermore, blocking Trim21 function through CD4 + T cell-targeting extracellular vesicles carrying RING domain-deficient Trim21 suppresses Th17 cell generation, mitigating IBD. Our data indicate that Indole-induced Trim21 upregulation is crucial for Th17 cell generation in IBD and propose microbial interventions and Trim21 inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Prescribing cascades in people with type 2 diabetes: analyses of two representative routine healthcare databases
abstract: Abstract Background Prescribing cascades, defined as initiation of medications to treat adverse drug reactions caused by other medications, may contribute to polypharmacy in people with type 2 diabetes. We aimed to determine whether commonly used diabetes and cardiovascular medications were associated with subsequent initiation of treatments for their known adverse drug reactions, indicating potential prescribing cascades. Methods We conducted two parallel cohort studies using prescription sequence symmetry analysis to assess asymmetry in the initiation sequence of index medications and corresponding marker medications. Twelve index-marker medication dyads were selected a priori from published literature. Data were obtained from the Scottish Diabetes Research Network national diabetes registry and the Welsh Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank between January 2015 and December 2023. Adults aged 40 years or older with type 2 diabetes were eligible if they had incident use of both an index and marker medication within a 365-day period. Adjusted sequence ratios comparing initiation of marker medications after versus before index medications were calculated after adjustment for secular prescribing trends. Ratios greater than 1.0 indicated potential prescribing cascades. Sensitivity analyses examined age, sex, socioeconomic position, comorbidity, and shorter observation windows (90 and 180 days). Estimates from both datasets were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Results A total of 387,338 individuals from the Scottish Diabetes Research Network and 296,582 from the Welsh Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank were eligible. Seven of 12 medication dyads showed evidence of prescribing cascades: sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors followed by urinary tract infection antibiotics (pooled adjusted sequence ratio 1.14, 95% confidence interval 1.10–1.17), antifungals (1.64, 1.58–1.69), and overactive bladder medications (1.16, 1.00-1.34); thiazolidinediones followed by loop diuretics (2.23, 1.28–3.89); calcium channel blockers followed by loop diuretics (1.80, 1.46–2.23); and statins followed by overactive bladder medications (1.32, 1.02–1.73) and hypnotics (1.45, 1.29–1.62). Findings were directionally consistent across demographic and clinical subgroups. Conclusions Prescribing cascades appear to be important contributors to polypharmacy among people with type 2 diabetes. Recognition of adverse drug reactions as a cause of new symptoms may identify opportunities to stop or modify the causative medication where appropriate, potentially reducing treatment burden and polypharmacy.

title: Altered brain activity and childhood trauma associate with gene and neurotransmitter patterns in transgender women with gender dysphoria
abstract: Abstract Background Although early-life stress and trauma may influence cortical development and increase vulnerability to gender dysphoria (GD), the relationship between brain function and childhood traumatic experiences in GD remains unexplored. This study aims to investigate the neurobiological mechanisms underlying GD by examining functional brain alterations and their associations with childhood trauma, neurotransmitter systems, and gene expression patterns. Methods This study recruited 44 transgender women (TW), 40 cisgender male, and 42 cisgender female controls. Participants were assessed using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) and Gender Identity/Gender Dysphoria Questionnaire for Adolescents and Adults (GIDYQ-AA), while resting-state fMRI data were analyzed for amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional ALFF (fALFF) measures. The transcriptional data were sourced from the Allen Human Brain Atlas. The JuSpace toolbox was used to investigate the atlas-based nuclear imaging-derived neurotransmitter maps. Results Compared to cisgender controls, TW showed decreased ALFF in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) but increased ALFF in the cerebellar lobule IX. TW exhibited decreased fALFF in the right PCC compared to cisgender women. TW also reported higher CTQ total and subscale scores. Notably, CTQ total and its subscale scores [emotional abuse and emotional neglect (EN)] were positively correlated with increased ALFF in the PCC. Multivariate regression analysis further revealed that interactions between fALFF value of the right PCC × CTQ total and fALFF value of the right PCC × EN independently predicted GIDYQ-AA scores in TW. The abnormal brain activity in TW was linked to genes enriched in mRNA catabolism and synaptic function, and was correlated with dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmission. Conclusions TW involves the PCC hypofunction and the cerebellar hyperactivation, synergistically modulated by childhood trauma, especially emotional neglect. These neural alterations are linked to gene regulatory and neurotransmitter pathways, revealing a multilevel neurophysiological framework of TW.

title: Impact of a lifestyle intervention for weight loss on liver-related outcomes in adults with obesity: a subanalysis of a clinical trial
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a structured weight-loss intervention on liver steatosis and liver stiffness in adults with obesity. Methods Post hoc analysis of prospectively collected data from a randomized crossover trial (NCT05420311) assessing changes in liver-related outcomes measured from baseline to three months during the overall sequential lifestyle intervention in adults with obesity. Participants sequentially followed a calorie-restricted standard diet, calorie-restricted ketogenic diet (KD), or modified alternate day fasting (mADF)—one month per diet—. Changes in controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness measurement (LSM) and estimated steatosis/LSM-based fibrosis risk categories assessed by vibration-controlled transient elastography were evaluated from baseline to three months during the overall sequential lifestyle intervention. Other assessments included changes in liver enzymes, anthropometric, and cardiometabolic parameters. Results Seventy-six participants were included in this subanalysis. Mean weight loss was 7.6 ± 4.7 kg at the end of the study period. Significant reductions in CAP and LSM from baseline to 3 months were observed (from 286.6 ± 70.7 dB/m to 256.6 ± 57.1, p < 0.001, and from 8.8 ± 6.0 kPa to 6.9 ± 3.5 kPa, p = 0.012, respectively). In addition, a significant reduction in the percentage of patients with liver steatosis and LSM-based fibrosis risk ≥F2 was observed. Significant decreases in serum levels of liver enzymes (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and gamma-glutamyl transferase) were also detected. Conclusions A structured weight-loss lifestyle intervention may be associated with improvements in non-invasive liver-related outcomes in adults with obesity. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05420311).

title: Multi-omics signatures of 8-year trajectories and heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease reveal serum citramalic acid as a key contributor
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a heterogeneous condition, yet early predictors for risk stratification remained limited. We aimed to identify multi-omics features predicting MASLD progression and heterogeneity. This population-based cohort study included 1694 participants from the Guangzhou Nutrition and Health Study. Gut metagenomics and targeted fecal and serum metabolomics were profiled. MASLD severity was defined using MRI-derived hepatic steatosis, and 8-year MASLD trajectories were assessed using repeated ultrasound examinations. We identified 9 microbial species, 13 fecal metabolites, and 13 serum metabolites associated with MASLD severity, with serum citramalic acid emerged as the top-ranked feature. For 8-year MASLD trajectories, microbial-, fecal-, and serum metabolite-based risk scores predicted MASLD incidence (per-SD HRs: 1.04, 1.18, and 1.21) and showed stronger associations with persistent MASLD (per-SD ORs: 1.27, 1.62, and 2.23). Multi-omics clustering further revealed three MASLD subtypes with distinct metabolic profiles. Metabolic dysfunction progressively worsened from Subtype A to Subtype C ( P trend < 0.05), with Subtype C exhibiting increased T2D risk (OR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.61–4.55). Key findings were replicated in an external validation cohort. Furthermore, citramalic acid administration in HFD-fed mice exacerbated metabolic dysfunction and hepatic steatosis, and disrupted hepatic pathways involved in lipid metabolism and cellular stress responses. Our study identified multi-omics features underlying MASLD progression and heterogeneity, providing early biomarkers for risk stratification and potential precision prevention of MASLD.

title: Urinary TAGMe methylation enables preoperative risk stratification and reveals enhancer‑mediated regulation in urothelial carcinoma
abstract: Accurate risk stratification in urothelial carcinoma (UC) remains challenging due to marked molecular heterogeneity, underscoring the potential value of non‑invasive biomarkers for improving risk stratification. TAGMe is an intergenic urinary DNA methylation marker that we previously developed for UC detection. Here, we investigated its potential value for preoperative prognostic stratification and explored its underlying biological function in UC. Preoperative urinary TAGMe methylation was measured by methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme quantitative PCR in 375 patients with UC and analyzed in relation to clinicopathological features and survival outcomes using Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression analyses. TAGMe was integrated with conventional clinicopathological variables to develop prognostic models and a nomogram, which were evaluated using the concordance index and time-dependent ROC analysis. Multi-omics analyses integrating ATAC-seq, Hi-C, ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN, and TCGA data were used to characterize the regulatory properties of the TAGMe locus. Dual-luciferase, DNA demethylation, and gain-of-function experiments were subsequently performed to validate TAGMe enhancer activity and investigate the functional role of BHLHE40-AS1. Preoperative TAGMe levels were associated with adverse pathological features and poorer recurrence-free, progression-free, and overall survival. Incorporating TAGMe into a prognostic nomogram improved risk discrimination beyond conventional clinicopathological variables and refined stratification within established pathological subgroups. Integrative epigenomic analyses revealed that TAGMe resides within an active enhancer‑like region marked by H3K27ac and H3K4me1 and physically interacts with the lncRNA BHLHE40‑AS1 locus. TAGMe activated BHLHE40‑AS1 transcription in a methylation‑dependent manner, and TAGMe hypermethylation correlated with reduced BHLHE40‑AS1 expression. Functional assays demonstrated that BHLHE40‑AS1 suppresses proliferation, migration, and epithelial–mesenchymal transition in bladder cancer cells. Urinary TAGMe methylation may complement conventional clinicopathological factors for preoperative risk stratification in UC, while the methylation-sensitive TAGMe–BHLHE40-AS1 enhancer axis provides a mechanistic link between intergenic DNA methylation and tumor progression.

title: Assessing the impact of additional inclusion criteria on the representativeness of EHR-based long COVID cohorts identified using U09.9
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are widely used to study Long COVID, yet cohort inclusion criteria may systematically affect cohort composition, shaping how findings are interpreted and to whom they may generalize. We analyzed harmonized EHR data from N3C among nondeceased individuals with at least one U09.9 Long COVID diagnosis between October 2021 and October 2023. Within this U09.9-identified cohort, we evaluated three additional inclusion criteria: COVID-19 diagnosis, likely COVID-19–related hospitalization, and availability of ≥ 2 years of prior medical history. Mixed-effects logistic or multinomial regression models estimated associations between selection criteria and sex, race/ethnicity, area-level poverty, and health insurance coverage, while zero-inflated negative binomial models evaluated estimates of healthcare utilization. Data-contributing partner was included as a random effect for all models. Sensitivity analyses examined regional variation and compared findings with COVID-19–only cohort. Cohort size, demographic composition, and healthcare utilization varied substantially by inclusion criteria. Requiring ≥ 2 years of medical history increased representation of women and individuals with higher outpatient utilization but reduced inclusion of individuals from low–insurance coverage areas. COVID-19–related hospitalization was associated with higher inpatient and non-inpatient utilization (acute care clinic visits, emergency room visits) and increased representation of non-Hispanic Black individuals, but lower representation of women. Having a documented COVID-19 diagnosis enriched cohorts with patients from higher-poverty and lower–insurance coverage areas and with greater healthcare utilization. Multinomial models showed that medical history requirements were negatively associated with inclusion of all non-White racial/ethnic groups. Findings were largely consistent across geographic regions and aligned with patterns observed in the COVID-19–only cohort. Routinely used EHR-based inclusion criteria are not analytically neutral. In N3C, cohort composition reflects site participation, data harmonization, common data model implementation, and data quality processes. Although these features are N3C-specific, similar design considerations may affect disparities and generalizability across EHR-based Long COVID research.

title: T cells in AML: are they functionally impaired? a call for comprehensive characterization
abstract: Abstract Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive cancer marked by uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid blasts in the bone marrow (BM). Management of newly diagnosed AML is guided by patient fitness and molecular risk stratification, incorporating intensive chemotherapy (IC), venetoclax-based regimens, targeted therapies, and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in selected patients (allo-HSCT). Despite initial responses, frequent relapses lead to a five-year survival rate below 30%. A factor linked to AML relapse is T cell exhaustion/dysfunction, especially after stem cell transplantation. Main body T cell exhaustion is often assessed solely based on the expression of inhibitory receptors which provides an incomplete picture of T cell impairment. We propose a more comprehensive and standardized definition of T cell functionality that extends beyond inhibitory receptor expression. This should encompass cytokine secretion and cytotoxic capacity, activation and proliferative potential, metabolic profile, T cell subset composition, telomere length, and epigenetic state. Additionally, we examine how the AML tumor microenvironment can lead to T cell impairment and based on emerging data we argue that T cells in AML are not uniformly dysfunctional. Conclusion A deeper and more comprehensive understanding of T cell functional heterogeneity in AML—based on standardized, multidimensional assessments rather than inhibitory receptor expression alone—is essential for advancing immunotherapy in this disease. Recognizing that T cells in AML are not uniformly dysfunctional but instead exhibit context-dependent impairment shaped by the tumor microenvironment, challenges prevailing assumptions and opens new therapeutic opportunities. Integrating functional, metabolic, and epigenetic insights into T cell profiling will be critical for the rational design, timing, and optimization of T cell–based therapies, with the potential to overcome immune failure and improve durable disease control in AML.

title: Machine learning predicts weight change in a real-world digital health application
abstract: Abstract Background Digital health applications offer scalable support for weight loss, but individual outcomes and retention vary substantially. It remains unclear how predictive information evolves during treatment, whether app engagement adds predictive information beyond early weight response, and whether the same factors predict weight loss and retention. Methods Using real-world data from the 12-week digital health application Oviva Direkt for Obesity , we developed machine learning models to predict clinically meaningful weight loss, continuous relative weight change, and full app retention. Weight-change and full-retention analyses included 17,953 and 26,714 adults, respectively. Models evaluated baseline characteristics, 4-week weight, and weekly app engagement metrics separately and in combination to quantify their incremental predictive value and assess how performance changed when early-treatment information was added to pretreatment characteristics. Results Baseline characteristics alone showed limited discrimination for clinically meaningful weight loss at weeks 8 and 12 (ROC AUC 0.54–0.58). Adding 4-week weight substantially improved performance (ROC AUC 0.86–0.92), whereas app engagement alone yielded modest improvements (ROC AUC 0.63–0.67). Adding app engagement to models including 4-week weight provided little further improvement (ROC AUC 0.87–0.92). A similar pattern was observed for continuous weight-change prediction. In contrast, full-retention prediction improved from ROC AUC 0.81 with baseline characteristics to 0.90 with app engagement, while 4-week weight provided no additional benefit. Weight-loss prediction was driven primarily by baseline weight, 4-week weight, and self-defined target weight, whereas engagement-related variables like goal setting and personalized logging recommendations were more influential for full retention. Conclusions Predictive performance for weight-loss outcomes improved substantially when information from the first four weeks, particularly 4-week weight, was incorporated. Accordingly, the week 8 and week 12 models should be interpreted as predictions updated during treatment rather than predictions based solely on pretreatment characteristics. Weight-loss response and sustained intervention use were characterized by distinct predictive information and may require different forms of early, targeted support. These findings provide a basis for further research on the early identification of individuals at risk of suboptimal outcomes and the development of more personalized digital obesity care. External validation in independent, relevant cohorts is required before the models can be considered for clinical implementation.

title: Optimizing precision lung cancer screening using willingness-to-pay–anchored risk eligibility thresholds
abstract: Abstract Background Despite the proven benefits of low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in lung cancer management, uptake remains limited due to cost. This study applies a structured decision-analytic framework to optimize LDCT screening through risk-based strategies in Singapore compared with conventional LDCT (based on age and smoking history) and no screening. Methods We developed a lifetime Markov model to simulate costs and outcomes for Singaporean smokers and never-smokers with a family history of lung cancer, stratified by sex. Transition probabilities and costs were informed by local data, with utilities from published sources. Screening strategies varied by start age (50, 55, 60) and frequency (annual, biennial, triennial). Outcomes included costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), discounted at 3% annually. Using a validated local risk prediction model, reverse threshold analyses identified optimal risk cut-offs for cost-effective screening, supported by deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses across willingness-to-pay thresholds of Singapore dollars (SGD) 45,000–75,000/QALY. Results Among smokers, annual risk-based screening from age 50 at 1-year risk thresholds of ≥ 0.37% for males and ≥ 0.51% for females produced the greatest health gains (ΔQALYs vs. no screening: 0.201 and 0.198, respectively), while the same risk-based annual screening from age 60 was most economically efficient (ΔQALYs: 0.177 and 0.182; incremental ICERs: SGD 40,155/QALY and SGD 42,666/QALY, respectively). Among never-smokers with a family history of lung cancer, conventional LDCT was not cost-effective; annual risk-based screening from age 50 in males at 1-year risk threshold of ≥ 0.16% and females at ≥ 0.21% maximized health gains (ΔQALYs: 0.013 and 0.021, respectively), while less intensive screening from age 60–biennial in males at 1-year risk ≥ 0.20% and triennial in females at ≥ 0.21%–was more economically efficient (ΔQALYs: 0.007 and 0.011; incremental ICERs: SGD 73,548/QALY and SGD 26,953/QALY, respectively). Conclusions Risk-based LDCT screening may improve screening efficiency and health gains while maintaining good value for money, with different screening intensities offering implementation options under varying budget constraints, though further research is needed to support its implementation in practice. These findings provide evidence to inform risk-based screening eligibility and implementation strategies, particularly in Asia with a high burden of lung cancer among never-smokers.

title: Diagnostic performance of cerebrospinal fluid examination in cases with suspected acute meningitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Bacterial meningitis is a severe disease with high morbidity and mortality, in which urgent diagnosis and treatment can improve the prognosis. The diagnosis relies heavily on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination, but the value of different CSF parameters has not been adequately studied. In preparation for the World Health Organization guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and care we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic accuracy of commonly used CSF parameters (Gram stain, leukocyte count and differential, glucose, total protein, and lactate) for the diagnosis of bacterial meningitis. The outcomes were sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value, likelihood ratios and area-under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC). A total of 27 studies with 5,673 patients were included. CSF Gram stain had an overall sensitivity of 85% (95% confidence interval [CI] 55–96%) with a 99% specificity. Per pathogen the sensitivity varied with 93% for Streptococcus pneumoniae , 30–89% for Neisseria meningitidis , 10–25% for Listeria monocytogenes , and 25–65% for Haemophilus influenzae . CSF leukocyte count had a sensitivity of 77% (95% CI 74–81%) and specificity of 83% (95% CI 75–92%), CSF neutrophil count 82% (95% CI 70–94%) and 84% (95% CI 77–90%), CSF glucose 66% (95% CI 52–79%) and 85% (95% CI 72–98%), CSF to blood glucose ratio 88% (95% CI 83–93%) and 78% (95% CI 52–100%), CSF total protein 86% (95% CI 80–92%) and 79% (95% CI 70–88%) and CSF lactate 94% (95% CI 91–98%) and 86% (95% CI 74–98%), respectively. CSF Gram stain has a high specificity, with varying but mostly moderate sensitivity per pathogen. An elevated CSF leukocyte count, specifically neutrophils, CSF protein concentration and CSF lactate are predictive of bacterial meningitis. Furthermore, a decreased CSF glucose concentration and low CSF to blood glucose ratio are also predictive of bacterial meningitis. Further studies are needed to assess combinations of these tests and novel biomarkers to improve diagnostic accuracy.

title: A novel murine colorectal cancer cell line mirroring key clinically relevant mutations
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a highly prevalent and lethal disease, with tumor heterogeneity contributing to varied responses to standard therapies. Preclinical models are essential for developing new strategies, yet existing models are limited in the specific tumor subtypes that they represent. To address this, we established a novel murine CRC cell line that represents tumors with mutations in Kras , Apc and Trp53 , the three most common mutations in human CRC. These novel cells, which we termed KAP, give rise to highly aggressive, invasive rectal tumors when implanted orthotopically. KAP cells were developed from colorectal organoids derived from mice harboring the oncogenic Kras G12D mutations as well as deletion of Trp53 . Organoids were further modified to knockout Apc using CRISPR-Cas9. KAP cells from organoids were grown on tissue culture treated flasks and used in a murine orthotopic rectal model using syngeneic B6 mice. KAP tumors were analyzed by immunohistochemistry to assess structural and cellular features of the tumor microenvironment. Additionally, to assess whether KAP tumors also mimic treatment response, we administered FOLFOX and radiation, standard therapies for CRC. We determined that KAP tumors recapitulate key features of human CRC, including poorly differentiated gland-like structures, dense areas of collagen deposition, immature vasculature, and a low abundance of intratumoral immune cells. This tumor microenvironment closely resembles immune-excluded CRC, a subtype known for its resistance to therapy. Importantly, following administration of standard therapy to mice bearing KAP rectal tumors, we observed similar outcomes to those seen in patients. The establishment of this novel cell line enhances the translational relevance of murine studies for CRC and provides a valuable tool for studying tumor biology and the therapeutic response in the context of low immune infiltration.

title: Short-term inverse association between changes in government expenditure on retail pharmaceuticals and treatable mortality in Spain
abstract: Specific studies on the relationship between pharmaceutical expenditure and mortality are sparse, particularly those that consider mortality from causes most sensitive to medical treatments (treatable mortality). The purpose was to assess short-term associations between changes in government expenditure on retail pharmaceuticals (GERP) and other health goods/services (GEOH) and changes in premature and non-premature mortality by avoidability and cause-groups in Spain. A cross-sectional time series design was used with annual data from 17 Spanish regions during 2001–2019. Outcomes were age-sex-standardized rates for premature (< 75 years) and non-premature (≥ 75 years) mortality stratified by avoidability (treatable, preventable, and non-avoidable), by cause-groups (circulatory, neoplastic, respiratory, infectious, and other causes) and jointly by avoidability and cause-groups. Using weighted log-log first-difference regression adjusted for relevant covariates, we estimated mortality elasticities with respect to GERP and GEOH, interpreted as the percentage change in mortality rate associated with a 1% increase in the two-year mean change in expenditure. A sub-analysis (2001–2013) additionally adjusted for government social expenditure (GSE). For GERP, significant negative elasticities ( p < 0.05) were observed for premature treatable mortality (− 0.23%) and for premature mortality from respiratory (− 0.56%), infectious (− 0.49%), and circulatory causes (− 0.22%), and also for non-premature treatable mortality (− 0.20%) and for non-premature mortality from infectious (− 0.66%) and respiratory causes (− 0.50%). In jointly-stratified analyses by avoidability and cause-groups, the largest inverse associations were observed for premature treatable mortality from infectious (− 1.60%) and respiratory causes (− 0.88%). For GEOH, elasticities were generally statistically nonsignificant and weaker, except for non-premature mortality from certain causes (e.g. circulatory) and particularly with one-year lag GEOH. In the GSE-adjusted sub-analysis, negative elasticities for non-premature mortality with respect to GERP weakened considerably. Short-term changes in GERP were inversely associated with changes in premature mortality, particularly from treatable causes, especially respiratory and infectious ones. For non-premature mortality, associations attenuated after GSE adjustment.

title: Genetic architecture of schizophrenia clinical subtype
abstract: Abstract Background Clinical heterogeneity in schizophrenia (SZ) presents a significant challenge to genetic research, as diverse symptom profiles may stem from distinct genetic risk factors. Although previous studies have stratified patients into symptom-based subtypes, and preliminary evidence suggests the presence of distinct architectures, these findings remain limited. This study aimed to identify the clinically defined SZ subtypes and investigate the genetic architecture underlying different subtypes. Methods In a Chinese Han cohort of 2,410 SZ patients, we applied K-means cluster analysis to symptom profiles to identify clinical subtypes. The identified subtype structure was validated in an independent cohort of 480 patients. Subsequently, subtype-specific genome-wide association studies (GWAS) were conducted to identify genetic risk loci associated with individual subtypes. Results Three stable subtypes were identified: Cluster-L (low severity), Cluster-S (severe), and Cluster-N (predominant negative symptoms). Reproducibility of this classification was confirmed in the independent cohort. The three subtypes also exhibited significantly different symptom network structures. In GWAS analysis, A total of four genome-wide significant loci were detected, including a Cluster-N–specific locus within the CNTN2 gene (lead SNP rs3767295, P = 5.30E-10, OR = 0.62). Gene-based analyses revealed additional risk genes unique to particular subtypes. Moreover, subtype-specific patterns emerged in both pathway-specific polygenic risk scores (pPRS) and cell type–specific PRS (ctPRS). Conclusions These findings underscore the value of patient stratification in improving statistical power to detect subtype-specific risk loci. They further demonstrate that SZ patients with distinct symptom profiles harbor differential genetic liabilities involving diverse biological pathways and cell types.

title: Ultra-processed food indices and component food groups in relation to incident type 2 diabetes and cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Broad ultra-processed food (UPF) measures combine product groups that may differ in cardiometabolic relevance. This study examined questionnaire-observable processing-related food groups, sweet-tasting beverage subtypes and dietary difference indices in relation to type 2 diabetes and cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
